# So should we trust academia?

By this point, we have learned a little bit about truth, models, systems, and dogma.

Perhaps "should we trust academia?" isn't the correct question. Maybe instead we should be asking how much we should trust academia, or when we should trust academia.

In this regard, I think the answer is context-dependent and subjective. The primary point that I think should be considered is whether academia is able to update in response to new information.
Research in many areas follows this exactly, which is why it can feel like researchers don't know what they are talking about.
Remember that believing we know something exactly, with no uncertainty at all, is dogma. Another important point is that a consensus built on research represents
high certainty based on evidence. Academic institutions are not a monolith, so consensus is one of the most valuable pieces of evidence that we have.
If research results hold up consistently regardless of which institution produces them, then we can be confident that we are heading in the right direction.
